title: The commute
venue: the coast community-college paper, Newport · the laundromat digest
logline: Twenty minutes home. The novel is still in the car.

panels.composition: 101 south, late afternoon. The Datsun. The sea on the right now.

image.prompt: an old Datsun driving south on a coastal highway behind a log truck, the gray Pacific on the right, late afternoon, brush-pen black and white

panels.composition: Wood, driving, talking to the passenger seat.

balloons.text: Chapter one. A man returns to the town he never left. No — a man never leaves the town he was returning to. No.

image.prompt: close-up of a young man driving and talking to the empty passenger seat, working something out

panels.composition: The log truck's load ahead. Cedar. He watches it instead.

image.prompt: close-up through a windshield of the back of a log truck loaded with cedar logs on a coastal highway

panels.composition: The Datsun pulling in behind the tavern at dusk — no, behind his parents' house. The garage doesn't exist yet. He sits in the car a minute with the engine off.

characters.pose: sitting in the parked car, engine off

image.prompt: an old Datsun parked in the driveway of a small coastal house at dusk, a young man sitting inside with the engine off, black and white, no words
image.notes: Not the garage yet. The garage apartment doesn't appear until 2004.

art.line: brush-pen now — the weekday deadline teaches the hand to commit; still xeroxed, still black and white
